A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a [[Definition:Measure Space|measure space]].
Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be non-negative [[Definition:Measurable Function|measurable functions]].
Then:
:$\displaystyle \int \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n \rd \mu \le \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$

B_source.statement:
Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be non-negative [[Definition:Measurable Function|measurable functions]] with $f_n \uparrow f$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu$

derived.g_n <= f_n pointwise: integral g_n <= integral f_n, so the liminf inequality

object_map.reformulation: Introduce the increasing auxiliary sequence g_n = inf_{k>=n} f_k, apply MCT to it, and compare to f_n.

validity_conditions: g_n = inf_{k>=n} f_k is nondecreasing in n and increases to liminf f_n, so MCT applies to (g_n).
g_n <= f_n pointwise, so integral g_n <= integral f_n.
Taking limits: integral liminf f_n = lim integral g_n <= liminf integral f_n.
proof_plan:
Let $g_n = \displaystyle \inf_{k \mathop \ge n} f_k$.
Then $\sequence {g_n}$ is an [[Definition:Increasing Sequence of Mappings|increasing]] sequence of non-negative measurable functions with:
:$g_n \uparrow \displaystyle \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n$

By the [[Monotone Convergence Theorem (Measure Theory)|Monotone Convergence Theorem]]:
:$\displaystyle \int g_n \rd \mu \to \int \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n \rd \mu$

As $g_n \le f_n$, by [[Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Monotone|monotonicity]]:
:$\displaystyle \int g_n \rd \mu \le \int f_n \rd \mu$
